fields.Participants: Analytics Manager, Category Mgr, VP Merchandising

Automation Opportunity: - Post-season analysis auto-assembled from the sales/markdown/forecast datasets; best/worst auto-ranked
Controls: - CTL-423 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Season Analysis & Learning (PA-64.3).)
- Operational: Analytics Manager methodology sign-off; Category Manager review before the playbook update
Pain Points / Risks: - **Attribution-to-weather risk**: a rainy-season category's performance is confounded by an unusually dry season (external factor, not planning error); mitigated by the weather-normalized view where the prior-year-same-season comparison controls for the seasonal-pattern baseline

- **Winner-confirmation-bias risk**: a "best performer" is confirmed for next year without examining whether it was the product or a one-off (a viral social-media moment); mitigated by the 2-season confirmation before locking an item into the playbook
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113, W208 retail analytics) — the post-season performance dataset
- Forecast/plan (links to VS-02 / W31 demand forecasting, VS-64 / W2382 assortment plan) — the plan baseline
- Markdown (links to VS-64 / W2390–W2397) — the markdown-rate input

steps.activity: Analyzes: seasonal sales vs. plan by category, SKU, store, region; sell-through rate; markdown rate; gross margin; identifies best and worst performing seasonal items

fields.Participants: Merch Planner, Analytics Manager, Category Mgr

Automation Opportunity: - MAPE auto-computed per SKU per season; systematic over/under-bias auto-flagged for the model update
Controls: - CTL-423 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Season Analysis & Learning (PA-64.3).)
- Operational: VP Merchandising sign-off on the forecast-model change
Pain Points / Risks: - **Model-overfit risk**: the forecast model is tuned to last season's outlier and over-corrects; mitigated by the multi-season rolling accuracy view (not single-season tuning)

- **New-SKU-no-baseline risk**: a first-year seasonal SKU has no prior-season baseline, making the forecast a guess; mitigated by the analogous-SKU proxy (a similar seasonal SKU's pattern as the baseline)
System Touchpoints: - Demand forecasting (links to VS-02 / W31, VS-64 / W2382) — the forecast and the actuals
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113) — the MAPE computation and pattern analysis
- Seasonal calendar (links to VS-29 / W306) — the season framing for the comparison
Time Estimate: ~2.5 days/season × 6 seasons = **~120–150 hours/year** Merch Planner + Analytics.

steps.activity: Compares: forecasted demand vs. actual sales per seasonal SKU; calculates forecast accuracy (MAPE); identifies systematic over/under-forecasting patterns; improves next season's forecast model

Automation Opportunity: - Seasonal-performance auto-rolled into the vendor scorecard; markdown-support-fulfillment auto-tracked from W2394
Controls: - CTL-423 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Season Analysis & Learning (PA-64.3).)
- CTL-48: rebate/markdown-dispute pattern as a scorecard input; operational: VP Merchandising review of any vendor recommended for tier-down on seasonal performance
Pain Points / Risks: - **Recency-bias risk**: a vendor's one bad season dominates the review despite a strong multi-season record; mitigated by the multi-season trend view in the scorecard

- **Sell-through-attribution risk**: a vendor's seasonal SKU sold through poorly due to BuildRight's pricing/display decisions, not the vendor's product; mitigated by the controlled attribution (controllable vs. non-controllable factors separated)
System Touchpoints: - Vendor scorecard (links to VS-67 / W2458, W2462) — the seasonal-performance feed into the scorecard
- Quality (links to VS-31 / W110) — the seasonal-quality dimension
- Markdown support (links to VS-64 / W2388, W2394) — the markdown-support-performance dimension
Time Estimate: ~2.5 days/season × 6 seasons = **~120–150 hours/year** Buyer + Category Manager (the file's 8–10 h/day convention).

steps.activity: Reviews vendor seasonal performance: on-time delivery, quality, sell-through of vendor's seasonal products, markdown support provided; feeds into vendor scorecard per VS-03

fields.Participants: CRM Mgr, Analytics Manager, Category Mgr

Automation Opportunity: - Segment/basket analysis auto-generated from the CDP; next-season targeting auto-suggested per segment
Controls: - CTL-423 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Season Analysis & Learning (PA-64.3).)
- CTL-423 (data-privacy — links to VS-91 / W53, RA 10173); operational: CRM Manager methodology sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Loyalty-bias risk**: the analysis covers only loyalty members (~600K) and misses the non-member seasonal shopper; mitigated by the member-vs-non-member basket comparison where the POS captures non-member transactions
- **Privacy risk**: the segment analysis uses customer purchase history; mitigated by the RA 10173 consent and anonymization per VS-91 / W53
System Touchpoints: - CRM/CDP (links to VS-13 / W17 loyalty, VS-126 CDP) — the loyalty-member seasonal-purchase data
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113) — the segment and basket analysis
- Marketing (links to VS-14 / W83 campaign) — the next-season targeting informed by the analysis

steps.activity: Analyzes: customer segments buying seasonal products, average basket with seasonal items, repeat seasonal purchase rate, channel preference for seasonal shopping; informs next season targeting

fields.Participants: Merch Planner, Analytics Manager, Store Design Mgr

Automation Opportunity: - Seasonal-zone productivity auto-computed; next-season zone-allocation auto-suggested
Controls: - CTL-423 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Season Analysis & Learning (PA-64.3).)
- Operational: Category Manager review of any seasonal-zone cut decision
Pain Points / Risks: - **Productivity-vs-experience risk**: a seasonal zone shows low sales/sqm but high dwell/experience value (a holiday-décor zone that builds brand even if not directly sold); mitigated by the dwell and conversion metrics alongside productivity
- **Format-conflation risk**: comparing the compact format's seasonal zone to the flagship's; mitigated by the within-format benchmarking
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113, VS-55 / W2169 space-productivity) — the seasonal-zone productivity
- Planogram (links to VS-55 / W314, VS-64 / W2384) — the seasonal display spec
- Traffic (links to VS-55 / W2178 heatmap) — the seasonal-zone traffic

steps.activity: Reviews: seasonal display zone productivity (sales/sqm) vs. standard zone; customer traffic in seasonal zones; display conversion rate; recommends zone allocation adjustments for next season

Automation Opportunity: - Markdown-effectiveness auto-computed per phase/depth; next-season strategy auto-suggested
Controls: - CTL-423 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Season Analysis & Learning (PA-64.3).)
- Operational: Category Manager + Finance joint sign-off on the strategy recommendation
Pain Points / Risks: - **Confounded-timing risk**: an "earlier markdown was better" finding is confounded by an earlier season-start or a stronger promo; mitigated by the controlled comparison (same season-stage, same promo context)

- **Margin-vs-clearance trade-off blindness**: a deeper markdown cleared inventory faster but at a margin loss that a shallower markdown would have avoided; mitigated by the margin-recovered vs. inventory-cleared dual view
System Touchpoints: - Pricing/markdown (links to VS-29 / W289, VS-64 / W2390–W2397) — the markdown dataset
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113) — the timing/depth effectiveness
- Forecast (links to VS-64 / W2399) — the forecast-vs-actual that informed the markdowns

steps.activity: Evaluates: markdown timing (was earlier markdown better?), depth (which discount level cleared inventory fastest?), phase progression effectiveness; recommends strategy improvements for next season

fields.Participants: FP&A Analyst, Finance Mgr, Category Mgrs, VP Merch

Automation Opportunity: - Seasonal-category P&L auto-assembled; variance-vs-plan and vs-prior-year auto-flagged
Controls: - CTL-423 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Season Analysis & Learning (PA-64.3).)
- CTL-423 (cost-of-goods and allowance accuracy — links to VS-158, VS-39); operational: CFO sign-off on the report
Pain Points / Risks: - **Allowance-timing-distortion risk**: the vendor allowance lands in a different period than the markdown, distorting the seasonal-category margin; mitigated by the allowance-accrual at markdown time (per W2397)
- **Category-confound risk**: a seasonal category's profitability is boosted by a non-seasonal SKU mis-classified into it; mitigated by the category-classification integrity check
System Touchpoints: - FP&A / cost accounting (links to VS-17 / W26, VS-158 / W85, VS-64 / W2397) — the seasonal-category P&L
- Plan (links to VS-101 merchandise financial planning, VS-64 / W2382) — the plan baseline
- Prior-year (links to VS-29 / W306 seasonal calendar) — the prior-year-same-season comparison

steps.activity: Calculates: seasonal category P&L (revenue, COGS, markdowns, vendor allowances, net margin); compares vs. plan and vs. prior year same season; identifies most/least profitable seasonal categories

fields.Participants: VP Merch, Category Mgrs, Merch Planners, Buyers
fields.Trigger: Annual update after all seasons reviewed

Automation Opportunity: - Playbook-change-diff auto-generated from the per-season learnings; playbook-references auto-linked to the W2382 planning kickoff
Controls: - CTL-423 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Season Analysis & Learning (PA-64.3).)
- Operational: COO sign-off on the annual playbook update; playbook referenced in the W2382 planning template
Pain Points / Risks: - **Playbook-as-shelfware risk**: the playbook is updated but not consulted at next year's planning (the learnings don't propagate); mitigated by the playbook referenced as the mandatory input at the W2382 seasonal-assortment-planning kickoff
- **Over-generalization risk**: a one-season outlier becomes a permanent playbook rule; mitigated by the 2-season confirmation threshold (per W2398) before a learning is promoted to the playbook
System Touchpoints: - Knowledge/playbook repository (links to VS-30 / W381 knowledge management, VS-88 document control) — the versioned playbook
- Analytics inputs (links to VS-64 / W2398–W2404) — the per-season learnings
- Merchandising planning (links to VS-01, VS-64 / W2382) — the consumers of the updated playbook
Time Estimate: ~7.5 days/year VP Merchandising + Category Mgr/Planner contributions absorbed = **~60–80 hours/year** VP Merchandising.

steps.activity: VP Merchandising compiles learnings from all 6 seasons into updated seasonal playbook: forecast adjustments, assortment changes, vendor recommendations, markdown strategy refinements, display improvements; distributes to planning team for next year
